start: ^Narrator: A woman in her early fifties looks up from a wall of access logs. Military bearing, and a mug of tea gone cold by the keyboard.
^Patricia Morgan: You'll be the consultant. Patricia Morgan, Chief Security Officer. Thanks for coming at short notice.
^Fill me in. What have you found so far?
^Skip the pleasantries. What access can you give me?
^I've been briefed. Quantum-safe keys, an inside job, and it ends tonight.

c-2: ^Patricia Morgan: Then we can skip a step.

briefing_details: ^Patricia Morgan: Data leaving the building. Four point two terabytes over six weeks.
^Patricia Morgan: Project Heisenberg. Quantum-safe key material for the national emergency dispatch rollout.
^Patricia Morgan: If ENTROPY gets the rest of it, people die waiting for ambulances that come too late.

c-0: ^Patricia Morgan: Transfer volumes. Two to four in the morning, out to an external host.
^Patricia Morgan: Three weeks to rule out legitimate remote work. Then I was told to stop looking.

suspects_overview: ^Patricia Morgan: Eight people with developed vetting in the cryptography division.
^Patricia Morgan: Dr Ruth Halloran leads the team. Five senior researchers, two junior engineers.
^Patricia Morgan: All vetted. All trusted. One of them shouldn't be.
^Can you get me in front of them without tipping anyone off?

c-0: ^Patricia Morgan: Already done. As far as the building knows, you're a routine security audit.
c-1: ^Patricia Morgan: I have a feeling. A feeling isn't evidence. That's your job.

provide_access: ^Patricia Morgan: Here. Visitor badge. It gets you through the front of the building and nowhere that matters.
^Patricia Morgan: Owen Gallagher in IT holds the spare cards. Dr Halloran's badge opens the server side. I can lean on either of them if you need me to.
^Patricia Morgan: My log of what's been flagged is on the desk. Take it.
^I'll find my own way from here.

c-0: ^Patricia Morgan: People. Someone in this building has noticed something and not said it. Then the servers.
^Patricia Morgan: When you think you have a name, bring me the why and the proof. Both.
c-1: ^Patricia Morgan: Bring me a name when you have one. With proof.

hub: ^How far did your own investigation get?
^I think I know who it is.
^You mentioned an email that stopped you. Can I see it?
^Anything else I should know before I go in?
^That's everything for now. I'll keep you posted.

c-6: ^Patricia Morgan: He's not a fighter. But cornered people surprise you. Keep the terminal between you and the door.
c-7: ^Patricia Morgan: Do. I don't like surprises.

ask_investigation: ^Patricia Morgan: It hit a wall. The access looks legitimate because it is legitimate. Whoever it is has every right to touch that data.
ceo_copy_handover: ^Patricia Morgan: I kept a copy. If this goes wrong, it went wrong there.
patricia_confession: ^Patricia Morgan: Between you and me? I should have pushed harder. I let a polite email stop me.
ask_suspects: ^Patricia Morgan: Dr Ruth Halloran, team lead. David Torres, cryptography lead. Amara Okafor and Tomasz Wierzbicki, the two best on the maths.
^Patricia Morgan: Hannah Leigh and Sanjay Rao. And two juniors, Ben Ashworth and Chloe Marsh. Ben does overnight test runs.

b:
^Patricia Morgan: Halloran's been fighting the CEO to publish the research. Ben's asked twice about a pay review. Torres has been distracted.

^Patricia Morgan: Angry, skint and distracted aren't evidence. I've been wrong about people before.

ask_company_politics: ^Patricia Morgan: The Home Office readiness review is in three weeks. The CEO, Jennifer Zhao, wants a clean file for it.
^Patricia Morgan: So: no press, no prosecution if it can be avoided, and no security incident on the record.

b: ^Patricia Morgan: I want it done properly. She wants it done quietly. Tonight we find out which of us wins.

request_authorization: ^I need the vetting files on the cryptography team.
^The server room wants a password Owen won't give me.

b: ^Patricia Morgan: Vetting files are restricted. Bring me a name or a pattern and I'll pull the ones that matter.

c-0: ^Patricia Morgan: That's what vetting will let me give you.
^Patricia Morgan: Read them properly. Nobody's file is as tidy as it looks.
c-1: ^Patricia Morgan: Owen holds IT's spare for every office. I'll message him now. On my authority.
^Patricia Morgan: If this turns out to be nothing, it was a routine audit. Understood?
c-2: ^Patricia Morgan: I sign the access log; IT holds the password. I'll message Owen and tell him it's on my authority.

share_findings_who: ^I've got a feeling. Nothing I can show you yet.

c-1: ^Patricia Morgan: Thursday at eight? The transfers run two till four, and he logged it with Owen. Try again.
c-3: ^Patricia Morgan: So have I. That's why you're here. Come back with evidence.

b: ^Patricia Morgan: Halloran was in Zurich the night that badge first went in. You've seen that. Try again.

accuse_halloran: ^Patricia Morgan: Ruth. Her spare, on the server hallway at two in the morning.
^Patricia Morgan: I've waited three weeks to do something. All right. I'll suspend her access and keep her in the lab until the police can talk to her.
^Patricia Morgan: If you're wrong, that's her career. And whoever it really is has just watched Security move.
torres_why: ^His own badge is on the server hallway those nights.
^He's been under strain. His wife's ill.
^Halloran says he's in her lab after hours, where the spare hangs.
^Check who comes in the front door just before the spare is used.
^Money. He's hiding how much he owes.
^He's the cryptography lead. He'd know how.

c-0: ^Patricia Morgan: Read it again. His badge never touches the server hallway. Hers does.
c-1: ^Patricia Morgan: Half this building has someone ill at home. That's not evidence.
c-2: ^Patricia Morgan: Her word, about her own badge. It's enough to look, not to act.
c-4: ^Patricia Morgan: That's why he might. It isn't proof that he did. Show me it leaving the building.
c-5: ^Patricia Morgan: That's how. I need why. People don't do this for nothing.
c-6: ^Patricia Morgan: So would seven other people. That's not evidence either.

log_reason_right: ^Patricia Morgan: ...His badge at the front door, then Ruth's spare at the server hallway six minutes on. Every night. And Ruth's own badge never comes in after seven.

b: ^Patricia Morgan: And Ruth's sitting in her lab, suspended on your word. That's on both of us now.

log_reason_right: ^Patricia Morgan: That's a pattern. It's not a reason, and it's not proof the data's going anywhere.

b: ^Patricia Morgan: It's enough to look in his office. I'll tell Owen you can have the spare.

significant_findings: ^Patricia Morgan: Slowly. I'm writing this down.

b: ^Patricia Morgan: Money. His wife's treatment isn't covered, and he's borrowed against the house.
^Patricia Morgan: His own journal. He knows what it costs, and he's doing it anyway.
^Patricia Morgan: The staging manifest on the research portal, in his name.
^Patricia Morgan: A staging manifest in the data centre. "Staged by: D. Torres."
^Patricia Morgan: The upload schedule names him as operator, on site. Tonight, half past eight.
^Patricia Morgan: And a firm called TalentStack ringing his desk.

significant_findings: ^Patricia Morgan: I sat three desks from him at the Christmas party. His kids drew on the tablecloth.

b: ^Patricia Morgan: And I suspended Ruth on your say-so. I'll have her access back on tonight. You can do your own apologising.

significant_findings: ^Patricia Morgan: Right. Your call from here. I'll keep the building quiet and the CEO out of your way.
^Patricia Morgan: His badge just went through the hallway and the vault's logged him in. He's at the upload terminal.

b: ^Patricia Morgan: I've told Owen you can have the spare for his office.
^Patricia Morgan: Stop him first. Then finish whatever you were doing on that research server. Your people will want all of it.
^Patricia Morgan: You've got his print, then. Good.
^Patricia Morgan: The data centre door reads his fingerprint. Something from his office will carry it.
^Patricia Morgan: You'll need his print for that door. His office first.

significant_findings: ^Patricia Morgan: When you've got him, keep him there and call me. I'll bring the police. They get him, and your evidence, without your name on it.
^Patricia Morgan: Be careful. Down there, you're on your own.
significant_close: ^And the badge log. Look at the main-entrance times.
^Whatever happens next is on me, not you.

c-0: ^Patricia Morgan: ...Six minutes before her spare, every night. You did read it properly.
c-2: ^Patricia Morgan: No. Some of it's on me. I let them stop me.
